blocks.c: Not to minus nine. To minus eleven, because that is where the lease is executed, and we knew that because page eleven says so, at the bottom, in a footer nobody reads:
Executed at the premises, Floor Zero, in the presence of the Landlord.

Minus eleven is not Floor Zero. Wen was very clear about this. Minus eleven is the last floor with a stair, and below minus eleven there is one more descent, and the freight car does it, and that is the only way down.

We stood in front of the freight car doors at minus eleven at nine minutes to six in the morning with two log books, a lease, eleven photographs, a woman on Hendry Street holding a signed and dated photograph in her car, and a plan that rested entirely on the difference between the words "a" and "the".
"Ravi," said Wen. "One thing before we get in."

"If it goes wrong, and it takes both of us, and one day some poor kid finds a key taped under a bracket." She looked at me. "Don't write SORRY on the tag. That's what I did and it made him careless, because he thought whoever left it was on his side and would help. Write something useful."
The freight car doors opened by themselves.
Inside, the brass panel had changed. Every button was gone: 31 through 1, B1, B2, all of them, blank brass with the ghosts of numbers.
There was one button, at the bottom, worn concave by fifty years of thumbs, and under it a small neat engraved plate that had definitely not been there on Tuesday.
